functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The only short external rotator innervated by the obturator nerve rather than the sacral plexus directly -- reflecting its more anterior/medial embryological grouping with the adductors.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Deep muscle belly around the outer surface of the obturator foramen/membrane, coursing posterolaterally beneath quadratus femoris to the trochanteric fossa
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: As part of the short lateral rotator group of the hip (with piriformis, obturator internus, and quadratus femoris), diffuse deep buttock and posterior hip pain, occasionally extending down the posterior thigh; the group has also been implicated when pain is lancinating into the vagina, rectum, scrotum, or posterior-superior thigh
trigger_points.notes: Travell & Simons and later manual-medicine summaries note that this small individual muscle's own referred-pain pattern is not well differentiated in the literature from that of piriformis, the other short lateral rotators, and the adductors -- it is described and treated as part of the group rather than with its own distinct trigger-point map
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in American Academy of Manual Medicine (AAMM), 'Gemellus Superior, Gemellus Inferior, and Obturator Externus' clinical summary (http://www.webmanmed.com/disorders/disorders_files/musclgd/hip/12756229.html), stating that per Travell & Simons it is difficult to distinguish the trigger-point referral of this short-lateral-rotator group from that of piriformis and the adductors
